cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I spent my Saturday fixing your fence. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you to next door. They've got six panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them three took my whole Saturday before you make me sound available for Sunday.

mechanism: A supervises the story of a completed fence repair but yields how B tells it to obtain recognition of the labor rather than more work.
confusable: Unlike soliciting jobs or compliments, A wants time and practical effort counted; borrowed authority negotiates testimony instead of commanding gratitude.
comparison: Referral language and resisting extra work differ from accepting unpacking and tea while asking a household to count trips.
seedUse: Use canonical D33-b Saturday/panels/referral chain and S02-b revising demands to keep the other person cooperative.
